label: gl-no-depth-buffer, after: the GL window asks for depth 0 and keeps its 8-bit stencil
kind: real-window GL probe, not a perf-suite capture (the suite never builds the GL surface)
machine: SPELDATOR, i7-14700K, RTX 4080 driver 610.62, Windows 11 26200, HDR display 4K at 150%, 120 Hz
configuration: Release (JIT), HULTUI_A11Y=0, SDL_WINDOW_ACTIVATE_WHEN_SHOWN=0, HULTUI_STARTUP=1, P-cores, idle-gated before every run, before and after alternating ABBA

memSaved.agreement: Task Manager, DXGI and nvidia-smi agree to 1 MiB

pixels.negativeControl: the same builds with stencil 0 as well: Junction and Vesper frames came out identical anyway (their stencil passes do not change those pixels), but the stencil scene differed in 111,883 px (sha 6FA2A09AF160A0CC): the non-antialiased star clip filled its whole rectangle and the translucent stroke blended twice where it crosses. So the scene sees a missing stencil, and depth 0 does not lose it.

results.sdlAttributesWindows: a hidden SDL window, nothing else: default depth gives depth 24 stencil 8, depth 0 gives depth 0 stencil 8 (WGL, NVIDIA)
